patient_has_finding_of_abdominal_pain_no.assessment: The chart explicitly states the patient presents with abdominal pain and describes her pain as localizing to the right lower quadrant at presentation.
patient_has_finding_of_abdominal_pain_no.evidence: A 15-year-old girl presents to the ER with abdominal pain. The pain appeared gradually and was periumbilical at first, localizing to the right lower quadrant over hours.

patient_has_finding_of_abdominal_pain_no.assessment: Chart states abdominal pain has localized to the right lower quadrant, which is synonymous with right lower abdominal pain.
patient_has_finding_of_abdominal_pain_no.evidence: The pain appeared gradually and was periumbilical at first, localizing to the right lower quadrant over hours.

patient_has_suspicion_of_acute_appendici.assessment: The clinical features (migration of pain, RLQ tenderness, loss of appetite) and ultrasound finding of an edematous appendix are classic for appendicitis, supporting a present suspicion of acute appendicitis.
patient_has_suspicion_of_acute_appendici.evidence: On examination, she has localized rebound tenderness over the right lower quadrant. On an abdominal ultrasound, a markedly edematous appendix is seen.

patient_presented_with_complaint_of_abdo.evidence: A 15-year-old girl presents to the ER with abdominal pain.

patient_presented_with_complaint_of_abdo.assessment: While initial pain was periumbilical, chart states pain localized to the right lower quadrant at presentation, so RLQ pain was part of her complaint on arrival.
patient_presented_with_complaint_of_abdo.evidence: The pain appeared gradually and was periumbilical at first, localizing to the right lower quadrant over hours.
